// while `&["a"]` or `&["div", "a"]` are okay.
let found_count = main_node.find.len;
assert_eq!;
```
*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support. This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.- *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.25.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.25.1

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

main_node.set_html;

# dom_query 0.25.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.25.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

assert_eq!;
// or:

/ which is more efficient.

use Document;
let html_contents = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
        <head><title>Test</title></head>
        <body>
            <div class="content">
            </div>
            <div class="remove-it">
                Remove me
            </div>
            <div class="replace-it">
                <div>Replace me</div>
            </div>
        </body>
    </html>"#;;
let doc = from;
let mut content_selection = doc.select;
// append a new html node to the selection
content_selection.append_html;
assert!;
// set a new content to the selection, replacing existing content
let mut set_selection = doc.select;
set_selection.set_html;
assert_eq!;
// remove the selection
doc.select.remove;
assert!;
// replace the selection with a new html, current selection will not change.
let mut replace_selection = doc.select;
replace_selection.replace_with_html;
assert_eq!;
//but the document will change
assert_eq!;
//instead of appending content, you can prepend it
let mut content_selection = doc.select_single;
// you can prepend one element or,
content_selection.prepend_html;
// more:
content_selection.prepend_html;
// Also you can insert html before selection:
let first = content_selection.select;
first.before_html;
// or after:
let third = content_selection.select;
third.after_html;
// now the added paragraphs standing in front of `div`
assert!;
// to set a text to the selection you can use `set_html` but `set_text` is preferable:
let p_sel = content_selection.select;

p_sel.set_text;

use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head></head>
<body>
    <div id="main">
        <p id="first">It's</p>
    </div>
</body>
</html>"#.into;
// selecting a node we want to attach a new element
let main_sel = doc.select_single;
let main_node = main_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// if you need just to create a simple element, then you can use the following:
let el = doc.tree.new_element;
// you still able to deal with element's attributes:
el.set_attr;
// and set text
el.set_text;
main_node.append_child;
// also main_node.append_child(&el);
assert!;
// because this method doesn't parse anything it is much more cheaper than following approaches.
// if you need to add a more complex element, you can use `node.append_html`,
// which is much more convenient, then previous approach:
main_node.append_html;
assert_eq!;
// There is also a `prepend_child` and `prepend_html` methods which allows
// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;
assert!;
// if we need to replace existing element content inside a node with a new one, then use `node.set_html`.
// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
// To completely replace contents of the node,
// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.
// Also we can specify more than one element in the string for methods
// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;
assert_eq!;

// This method is a much faster alternative to
// `doc.select("html > head > base").attr("href")`.

// it will traverse the tree again.
// The reason it is not cached is to keep `Document` implementing the `Send` trait.

// Also it is accessible from any node of the tree.
let base_uri = node.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support. This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.- *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.24.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.24.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

use Document;
use StrTendril;
// Document may consume &str, String, StrTendril

<html><head><title>Test Page</title></head><body></body></html>"#;

let contents_string = contents_str.to_string;
let doc = from;
let contents_tendril = from;
let doc = from;
// The root element for the `Document` is a Document
assert!;
// if the source has DocType, then the Document will also have one
// as a first child.
assert!;
//both of them are not elements.

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support. This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.- *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.23.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.23.1

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

let selected_count = doc.select.nodes.len;
assert_eq!;
// `find` currently can deal only with paths that start after the current node.
// In the following example, `&["html", "body", "div", "a"]` will fail,
// while `&["a"]` or `&["div", "a"]` are okay.
let found_count = main_node.find.len;
assert_eq!;
```
*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.

assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.23.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.23.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

use Document;

let el = doc.tree.new_element;

el.set_attr;

el.set_text;

// also main_node.append_child(&el);

// if you need to add a more complex element, you can use `node.append_html`,

main_node.append_html;

// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;

// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
// To completely replace contents of the node,
// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.
// Also we can specify more than one element in the string for methods
// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;

# dom_query 0.22.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.22.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

// this approach is consuming all nodes into vec at first, and then you can call `iter().next()` to get the first one.
let next_selection = doc.select.iter.next.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// currently, to get data from all matches you need to iterate over them, either:
let all_matched: String = selection.iter.map.collect;
assert_eq!;
// or:
let all_matched: String = selection.nodes.iter.map.collect;
/ which is more efficient.
assert_eq!;

use Document;
let html_contents = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
        <head><title>Test</title></head>
        <body>
            <div class="content">
            </div>

            </div>
        </body>
    </html>"#;;

// append a new html node to the selection
content_selection.append_html;
assert!;
// set a new content to the selection, replacing existing content
let mut set_selection = doc.select;
set_selection.set_html;
assert_eq!;
// remove the selection
doc.select.remove;
assert!;
// replace the selection with a new html, current selection will not change.
let mut replace_selection = doc.select;
replace_selection.replace_with_html;
assert_eq!;
//but the document will change
assert_eq!;
//instead of appending content, you can prepend it
let mut content_selection = doc.select_single;
// you can prepend one element or,
content_selection.prepend_html;
// more:
content_selection.prepend_html;
// Also you can insert html before selection:
let first = content_selection.select;
first.before_html;
// or after:
let third = content_selection.select;
third.after_html;
// now the added paragraphs standing in front of `div`

let p_sel = content_selection.select;

p_sel.set_text;

use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head></head>
<body>
    <div id="main">
        <p id="first">It's</p>
    </div>
</body>
</html>"#.into;
// selecting a node we want to attach a new element
let main_sel = doc.select_single;
let main_node = main_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// if you need just to create a simple element, then you can use the following:
let el = doc.tree.new_element;
// you still able to deal with element's attributes:
el.set_attr;
// and set text
el.set_text;
main_node.append_child;
// also main_node.append_child(&el);
assert!;
// because this method doesn't parse anything it is much more cheaper than following approaches.
// if you need to add a more complex element, you can use `node.append_html`,
// which is much more convenient, then previous approach:
main_node.append_html;
assert_eq!;
// There is also a `prepend_child` and `prepend_html` methods which allows
// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;
assert!;
// if we need to replace existing element content inside a node with a new one, then use `node.set_html`.
// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
// To completely replace contents of the node,
// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.
// Also we can specify more than one element in the string for methods
// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;
assert_eq!;

assert_eq!;

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.21.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.21.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

use Document;
use StrTendril;
// Document may consume &str, String, StrTendril
let contents_str = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html><head><title>Test Page</title></head><body></body></html>"#;
let doc = from;
let contents_string = contents_str.to_string;
let doc = from;
let contents_tendril = from;
let doc = from;
// The root element for the `Document` is a Document
assert!;
// if the source has DocType, then the Document will also have one
// as a first child.
assert!;
//both of them are not elements.

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.20.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.20.2

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

        <div id="main"></div>
    </body>
</html>"#.into;
let main_sel = doc.select_single;
let main_node = main_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// create 10 child blocks with links
let total_links = 10usize;
for i in 0..total_links
let selected_count = doc.select.nodes.len;
assert_eq!;
// `find` currently can deal only with paths that start after the current node.
// In the following example, `&["html", "body", "div", "a"]` will fail,
// while `&["a"]` or `&["div", "a"]` are okay.
let found_count = main_node.find.len;
assert_eq!;
```
*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.20.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.20.1

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

use Document;
let html_contents = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>

content_selection.prepend_html;

content_selection.prepend_html;
// Also you can insert html before selection:
let first = content_selection.select;
first.before_html;
// or after:
let third = content_selection.select;
third.after_html;
// now the added paragraphs standing in front of `div`

p_sel.set_text;

use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>

    </div>
</body>
</html>"#.into;

let main_sel = doc.select_single;
let main_node = main_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// if you need just to create a simple element, then you can use the following:
let el = doc.tree.new_element;
// you still able to deal with element's attributes:
el.set_attr;
// and set text
el.set_text;
main_node.append_child;
// also main_node.append_child(&el);
assert!;
// because this method doesn't parse anything it is much more cheaper than following approaches.
// if you need to add a more complex element, you can use `node.append_html`,
// which is much more convenient, then previous approach:
main_node.append_html;

// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;
assert!;
// if we need to replace existing element content inside a node with a new one, then use `node.set_html`.
// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
// To completely replace contents of the node,
// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.
// Also we can specify more than one element in the string for methods
// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;
assert_eq!;

</html>"#;

// This method is a much faster alternative to
// `doc.select("html > head > base").attr("href")`.

// it will traverse the tree again.
// The reason it is not cached is to keep `Document` implementing the `Send` trait.

let base_uri = node.base_uri.unwrap;

# dom_query 0.20.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.20.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

// but if you call inner_html() on it, you will get the inner_html of the first match:
assert_eq!;
//this approach is using the first node from nodes vec and `select_single` consumes one iteration instead.
let first_selection = doc.select.first;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// this approach is consuming all nodes into vec at first, and then you can call `iter().next()` to get the first one.
let next_selection = doc.select.iter.next.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// currently, to get data from all matches you need to iterate over them, either:
let all_matched: String = selection.iter.map.collect;
assert_eq!;
// or:
let all_matched: String = selection.nodes.iter.map.collect;
/ which is more efficient.
assert_eq!;

use Document;
let html_contents = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
        <head><title>Test</title></head>
        <body>
            <div class="content">
            </div>
            <div class="remove-it">
                Remove me
            </div>
            <div class="replace-it">
                <div>Replace me</div>
            </div>
        </body>
    </html>"#;;
let doc = from;
let mut content_selection = doc.select;
// append a new html node to the selection
content_selection.append_html;
assert!;
// set a new content to the selection, replacing existing content
let mut set_selection = doc.select;
set_selection.set_html;
assert_eq!;
// remove the selection
doc.select.remove;
assert!;
// replace the selection with a new html, current selection will not change.
let mut replace_selection = doc.select;
replace_selection.replace_with_html;
assert_eq!;
//but the document will change
assert_eq!;
//instead of appending content, you can prepend it
let mut content_selection = doc.select_single;
// you can prepend one element or,
content_selection.prepend_html;
// more:
content_selection.prepend_html;
// Also you can insert html before selection:
let first = content_selection.select;
first.before_html;
// or after:
let third = content_selection.select;
third.after_html;
// now the added paragraphs standing in front of `div`
assert!;
// to set a text to the selection you can use `set_html` but `set_text` is preferable:
let p_sel = content_selection.select;
let total_p = p_sel.length;
p_sel.set_text;
assert_eq!;

```
use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head></head>
<body>
    <div id="main">
        <p id="first">It's</p>
    </div>
</body>
</html>"#.into;
// selecting a node we want to attach a new element
let main_sel = doc.select_single;
let main_node = main_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// if you need just to create a simple element, then you can use the following:
let el = doc.tree.new_element;
// you still able to deal with element's attributes:
el.set_attr;
// and set text
el.set_text;
main_node.append_child;
// also main_node.append_child(&el);
assert!;
// because this method doesn't parse anything it is much more cheaper than following approaches.
// if you need to add a more complex element, you can use `node.append_html`,
// which is much more convenient, then previous approach:
main_node.append_html;
assert_eq!;
// There is also a `prepend_child` and `prepend_html` methods which allows
// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;
assert!;
// if we need to replace existing element content inside a node with a new one, then use `node.set_html`.
// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
// To completely replace contents of the node,
// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.
// Also we can specify more than one element in the string for methods
// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;
assert_eq!;

use Document;

// This method is a much faster alternative to
// `doc.select("html > head > base").attr("href")`.

// it will traverse the tree again.
// The reason it is not cached is to keep `Document` implementing the `Send` trait.

let sel = doc.select_single;
let node = sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// Also it is accessible from any node of the tree.
let base_uri = node.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.19.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.19.2

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

use Document;
use StrTendril;
// Document may consume &str, String, StrTendril
let contents_str = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html><head><title>Test Page</title></head><body></body></html>"#;
let doc = from;
let contents_string = contents_str.to_string;
let doc = from;
let contents_tendril = from;
let doc = from;
// The root element for the `Document` is a Document
assert!;
// if the source has DocType, then the Document will also have one
// as a first child.
assert!;
//both of them are not elements.

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.19.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.19.1

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

let extra_node = extra_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
assert!;
assert!;

## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.19.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.19.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

main_node.prepend_html;

// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;

// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.

main_node.replace_with_html;

# dom_query 0.18.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.18.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

// if you need to select only the first, single match, you can use following:
let single_selection = doc.select_single;
// access is only for the first matching:
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// simple selection contains all matches:
let selection = doc.select;
assert_eq!;
// but if you call inner_html() on it, you will get the inner_html of the first match:
assert_eq!;
//this approach is using the first node from nodes vec and `select_single` consumes one iteration instead.
let first_selection = doc.select.first;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// this approach is consuming all nodes into vec at first, and then you can call `iter().next()` to get the first one.
let next_selection = doc.select.iter.next.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// currently, to get data from all matches you need to iterate over them, either:
let all_matched: String = selection.iter.map.collect;
assert_eq!;
// or:
let all_matched: String = selection.nodes.iter.map.collect;
/ which is more efficient.
assert_eq!;

use Document;
let html_contents = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
        <head><title>Test</title></head>
        <body>
            <div class="content">
            </div>
            <div class="remove-it">
                Remove me
            </div>
            <div class="replace-it">
                <div>Replace me</div>
            </div>
        </body>
    </html>"#;;
let doc = from;
let mut content_selection = doc.select;
// append a new html node to the selection
content_selection.append_html;
assert!;
// set a new content to the selection, replacing existing content
let mut set_selection = doc.select;
set_selection.set_html;
assert_eq!;
// remove the selection
doc.select.remove;
assert!;
// replace the selection with a new html, current selection will not change.
let mut replace_selection = doc.select;
replace_selection.replace_with_html;
assert_eq!;
//but the document will change
assert_eq!;
//instead of appending content, you can prepend it
let mut content_selection = doc.select_single;
// you can prepend one element or,
content_selection.prepend_html;
// more:
content_selection.prepend_html;
// Also you can insert html before selection:
let first = content_selection.select;
first.before_html;
// or after:
let third = content_selection.select;
third.after_html;
// now the added paragraphs standing in front of `div`
assert!;
// to set a text to the selection you can use `set_html` but `set_text` is preferable:
let p_sel = content_selection.select;
let total_p = p_sel.length;
p_sel.set_text;

```
use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head></head>
<body>
    <div id="main">
        <p id="first">It's</p>
    </div>
</body>
</html>"#.into;
// selecting a node we want to attach a new element
let main_sel = doc.select_single;
let main_node = main_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// if you need just to create a simple element, then you can use the following:
let el = doc.tree.new_element;
// you still able to deal with element's attributes:
el.set_attr;
// and set text
el.set_text;
main_node.append_child;
// also main_node.append_child(&el);
assert!;
// because this method doesn't parse anything it is much more cheaper than following approaches.
// if you need to add a more complex element, you can use `node.append_html`,
// which is much more convenient, then previous approach:
main_node.append_html;
assert_eq!;
// There is also a `prepend_child` and `prepend_html` methods which allows
// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;
assert!;
// if we need to replace existing element content inside a node with a new one, then use `node.set_html`.
// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
// To completely replace contents of the node,
// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.
// Also we can specify more than one element in the string for methods
// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;
assert_eq!;

use Document;

// it will traverse the tree again.
// The reason it is not cached is to keep `Document` implementing the `Send` trait.

let sel = doc.select_single;

// Also it is accessible from any node of the tree.
let base_uri = node.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.17.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.17.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

use Document;
use StrTendril;
// Document may consume &str, String, StrTendril
let contents_str = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html><head><title>Test Page</title></head><body></body></html>"#;
let doc = from;
let contents_string = contents_str.to_string;
let doc = from;
let contents_tendril = from;
let doc = from;
// The root element for the `Document` is a Document
assert!;
// if the source has DocType, then the Document will also have one
// as a first child.
assert!;
//both of them are not elements.

let html = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head><title>Test</title></head>
    <body><input hidden="" id="k" class="important" type="hidden" name="k" data-k="100"></body>
</html>"#;
let doc = from;
let mut input_selection = doc.select;
// get the value of attribute "data-k"
let val = input_selection.attr.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
// remove the attribute "data-k" from the element
input_selection.remove_attr;
// get the value of attribute "data-k", if missing, return default value
let val_or = input_selection.attr_or;
assert_eq!;
// remove a list of attributes from the element
input_selection.remove_attrs;
// set a attribute "data-k" with value "200"
input_selection.set_attr;
assert_eq!;
// check if attribute "hidden" exists on the element
let is_hidden = input_selection.has_attr;
assert!;
let has_title = input_selection.has_attr;
assert!;
// remove all attributes from the element
input_selection.remove_all_attrs;
assert_eq!;

use Document;
let html_contents = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
        <head><title>Test</title></head>
        <body>
            <div class="content">
            </div>
            <div class="remove-it">
                Remove me
            </div>
            <div class="replace-it">
                <div>Replace me</div>
            </div>
        </body>
    </html>"#;;
let doc = from;
let mut content_selection = doc.select;
// append a new html node to the selection
content_selection.append_html;
assert!;
// set a new content to the selection, replacing existing content
let mut set_selection = doc.select;
set_selection.set_html;
assert_eq!;
// remove the selection
doc.select.remove;
assert!;
// replace the selection with a new html, current selection will not change.
let mut replace_selection = doc.select;
replace_selection.replace_with_html;
assert_eq!;
//but the document will change
assert_eq!;
//instead of appending content, you can prepend it
let mut content_selection = doc.select_single;
// you can prepend one element or,
content_selection.prepend_html;
// more:
content_selection.prepend_html;
// Also you can insert html before selection:
let first = content_selection.select;
first.before_html;
// or after:
let third = content_selection.select;
third.after_html;
// now the added paragraphs standing in front of `div`
assert!;
// to set a text to the selection you can use `set_html` but `set_text` is preferable:
let p_sel = content_selection.select;

p_sel.set_text;

```
use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head></head>
<body>
    <div id="main">
        <p id="first">It's</p>
    </div>
</body>
</html>"#.into;
// selecting a node we want to attach a new element
let main_sel = doc.select_single;
let main_node = main_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// if you need just to create a simple element, then you can use the following:
let el = doc.tree.new_element;
// you still able to deal with element's attributes:
el.set_attr;
// and set text
el.set_text;
main_node.append_child;
// also main_node.append_child(&el);
assert!;
// because this method doesn't parse anything it is much more cheaper than following approaches.
// if you need to add a more complex element, you can use `node.append_html`,
// which is much more convenient, then previous approach:
main_node.append_html;
assert_eq!;
// There is also a `prepend_child` and `prepend_html` methods which allows
// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;
assert!;
// if we need to replace existing element content inside a node with a new one, then use `node.set_html`.
// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
// To completely replace contents of the node,
// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.
// Also we can specify more than one element in the string for methods
// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;
assert_eq!;

use Document;
let contents: &str = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <base href="https://www.example.com/"/>
        <title>Test</title>
    </head>
    <body>
        <div id="main"></div>
    </body>
</html>"#;
let doc = from;
// This method is a much faster alternative to
// `doc.select("html > head > base").attr("href")`.
// Currently, it does not cache the result, so each time you call it,
// it will traverse the tree again.
// The reason it is not cached is to keep `Document` implementing the `Send` trait.
// It may be called from the document level.
let base_uri = doc.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
let sel = doc.select_single;
let node = sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// Also it is accessible from any node of the tree.
let base_uri = node.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
```
## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.16.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.16.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

use Document;

let doc = from;
let contents_tendril = from;
let doc = from;
// The root element for the `Document` is a Document
assert!;
// if the source has DocType, then the Document will also have one
// as a first child.
assert!;
//both of them are not elements.

use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head></head>
<body>
    <ul class="list">
        <li>1</li><li>2</li><li>3</li>
    </ul>
    <ul class="list">
        <li>4</li><li>5</li><li>6</li>
    </ul>
</body>
</html>"#
    .into;
// if you need to select only the first, single match, you can use following:
let single_selection = doc.select_single;
// access is only for the first matching:
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// simple selection contains all matches:
let selection = doc.select;
assert_eq!;
// but if you call inner_html() on it, you will get the inner_html of the first match:
assert_eq!;
//this approach is using the first node from nodes vec and `select_single` consumes one iteration instead.
let first_selection = doc.select.first;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// this approach is consuming all nodes into vec at first, and then you can call `iter().next()` to get the first one.
let next_selection = doc.select.iter.next.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// currently, to get data from all matches you need to iterate over them, either:
let all_matched: String = selection.iter.map.collect;
assert_eq!;
// or:
let all_matched: String = selection.nodes.iter.map.collect;
/ which is more efficient.
assert_eq!;

use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>Test</head>
    <body>
        <div id="great-ancestor">
            <div id="grand-parent">
                <div id="parent">
                    <div id="child">Child</div>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </body>
</html>
"#.into;
// selecting an element
let child_sel = doc.select;
assert!;
let child_node = child_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// getting all ancestors
let ancestors = child_node.ancestors;
let ancestor_sel = from;
// or just: let ancestor_sel = child_sel.ancestors(None);
// in this case ancestors includes all ancestral nodes including html
// the root html element is presented in the ancestor selection
assert!;
// also the direct parent of our starting node is presented
assert!;
// `Selection::is` matches only the current selection without descending down the tree,
// so it won't match the #child node.
assert!;
// if you don't require all ancestors, you can specify a number of ancestors you need -- `max_limit`
let ancestors = child_node.ancestors;
let ancestor_sel = from;
// in this case ancestors includes only two ancestral nodes: #grand-parent and #parent
assert!;
assert!;

## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.15.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.15.2

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

main_node.set_html;

# dom_query 0.15.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.15.1

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

        <li>1</li><li>2</li><li>3</li>
    </ul>
    <ul class="list">
        <li>4</li><li>5</li><li>6</li>
    </ul>
</body>
</html>"#
    .into;
// if you need to select only the first, single match, you can use following:
let single_selection = doc.select_single;
// access is only for the first matching:
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// simple selection contains all matches:
let selection = doc.select;
assert_eq!;
// but if you call inner_html() on it, you will get the inner_html of the first match:
assert_eq!;
//this approach is using the first node from nodes vec and `select_single` consumes one iteration instead.
let first_selection = doc.select.first;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// this approach is consuming all nodes into vec at first, and then you can call `iter().next()` to get the first one.
let next_selection = doc.select.iter.next.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// currently, to get data from all matches you need to iterate over them, either:
let all_matched: String = selection.iter.map.collect;
assert_eq!;
// or:
let all_matched: String = selection.nodes.iter.map.collect;
/ which is more efficient.
assert_eq!;
```

use Document;
let html_contents = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
        <head><title>Test</title></head>
        <body>
            <div class="content">
            </div>
            <div class="remove-it">
                Remove me
            </div>
            <div class="replace-it">
                <div>Replace me</div>
            </div>
        </body>
    </html>"#;;
let doc = from;
let mut content_selection = doc.select;
// append a new html node to the selection
content_selection.append_html;
assert!;
// set a new content to the selection, replacing existing content
let mut set_selection = doc.select;
set_selection.set_html;
assert_eq!;
// remove the selection
doc.select.remove;
assert!;
// replace the selection with a new html, current selection will not change.
let mut replace_selection = doc.select;
replace_selection.replace_with_html;
assert_eq!;
//but the document will change
assert_eq!;
//instead of appending content, you can prepend it
let mut content_selection = doc.select_single;
// you can prepend one element or,
content_selection.prepend_html;
// more:
content_selection.prepend_html;
// Also you can insert html before selection:
let first = content_selection.select;
first.before_html;
// or after:
let third = content_selection.select;
third.after_html;
// now the added paragraphs standing in front of `div`
assert!;
// to set a text to the selection you can use `set_html` but `set_text` is preferable:
let p_sel = content_selection.select;
let total_p = p_sel.length;
p_sel.set_text;
assert_eq!;

```
use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head></head>
<body>
    <div id="main">
        <p id="first">It's</p>
    </div>
</body>
</html>"#.into;
// selecting a node we want to attach a new element
let main_sel = doc.select_single;
let main_node = main_sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// if you need just to create a simple element, then you can use the following:
let el = doc.tree.new_element;
// you still able to deal with element's attributes:
el.set_attr;
// and set text
el.set_text;
main_node.append_child;
// also main_node.append_child(&el);
assert!;
// because this method doesn't parse anything it is much more cheaper than following approaches.
// if you need to add a more complex element, you can use `node.append_html`,
// which is much more convenient, then previous approach:
main_node.append_html;
assert_eq!;
// There is also a `prepend_child` and `prepend_html` methods which allows
// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;
assert!;
// if we need to replace existing element content inside a node with a new one, then use `node.set_html`.
// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
// To completely replace contents of the node,
// including itself use `node.replace_with_html`.
// Also we can specify more than one element in the string for methods
// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;
assert_eq!;

use Document;
let contents: &str = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>

// This method is a much faster alternative to
// `doc.select("html > head > base").attr("href")`.
// Currently, it does not cache the result, so each time you call it,
// it will traverse the tree again.
// The reason it is not cached is to keep `Document` implementing the `Send` trait.
// It may be called from the document level.
let base_uri = doc.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
let sel = doc.select_single;
let node = sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// Also it is accessible from any node of the tree.
let base_uri = node.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;

## Related projects

## Crate features

- `hashbrown`— optional,replaces standard hashmaps and hashsets with- `hashbrown`hashmaps and hashsets.
- `atomic`— optional, switches- `NodeData`from using- `StrTendril`to- `Tendril<tendril::fmt::UTF8, tendril::Atomic>`. This allows- `NodeData`and all ascending structures, including- `Document`, to implement the- `Send`trait;
- `markdown`— optional, enables the- `Document::md`and- `NodeRef::md`methods, allowing serialization of a document or node to- `Markdown`text.
- `mini_selector`— optional, provides a lightweight and faster alternative for element matching with limited CSS selector support.
 This includes additional- `NodeRef`methods:- `find_descendants`,- `try_find_descendants`,- `mini_is`, and- `mini_match`.
 - *This is an experimental feature that may change in future releases.*

# dom_query 0.15.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dom_query/0.15.0

# DOM_QUERY: A Flexible Rust Crate for DOM Querying and Manipulation

DOM_QUERY is a flexible Rust crate that simplifies HTML parsing, DOM querying and manipulation by providing a high-level jQuery-like API. It uses the `html5ever` crate for HTML parsing and the `selectors` crate for efficient DOM traversal and element selection.

## Features

- Parse HTML documents and fragments
- Query DOM elements using CSS selectors
- Traverse the DOM tree (ancestors, parents, children, siblings)
- Manipulate elements and their attributes:
- Add/remove/modify attributes
- Change element content
- Add/remove elements
- Rename elements
- Move elements within the DOM tree

[!NOTE] This crate is a significantly enhanced fork of

[nipper](https://crates.io/crates/nipper), featuring expanded CSS selector support, enhanced DOM traversal and improved DOM manipulation capabilities.

## Examples

use Document;
use StrTendril;
// Document may consume &str, String, StrTendril
let contents_str = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html><head><title>Test Page</title></head><body></body></html>"#;
let doc = from;
let contents_string = contents_str.to_string;
let doc = from;
let contents_tendril = from;
let doc = from;
// The root element for the `Document` is a Document
assert!;
// if the source has DocType, then the Document will also have one
// as a first child.
assert!;
//both of them are not elements.

use Document;
let doc: Document = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>

        <p id="first">It's</p>
    </div>

el.set_attr;

// which is much more convenient, then previous approach:
main_node.append_html;

// to insert content to the begging of the node.
main_node.prepend_html;

// It changes the inner html contents of the node.
main_node.set_html;

// like `replace_with_html`, `set_html` and `append_html`.
main_node.replace_with_html;
assert!;

use Document;
let contents: &str = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <base href="https://www.example.com/"/>
        <title>Test</title>
    </head>
    <body>

    </body>
</html>"#;
let doc = from;
// This method is a much faster alternative to
// `doc.select("html > head > base").attr("href")`.
// Currently, it does not cache the result, so each time you call it,
// it will traverse the tree again.
// The reason it is not cached is to keep `Document` implementing the `Send` trait.
// It may be called from the document level.
let base_uri = doc.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
let sel = doc.select_single;
let node = sel.nodes.first.unwrap;
// Also it is accessible from any node of the tree.
let base_uri = node.base_uri.unwrap;
assert_eq!;

*This example requires  markdown feature.*

```
use Document;
let contents = "
<style>p {color: blue;}</style>
<p>I really like using <b>Markdown</b>.</p>
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "I really like using **Markdown**\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = from;
// Passing `None` into md allows to use default skip tags, which are:
// `["script", "style", "meta", "head"]`.
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
// If you need the full text content of the elements, pass `Some(&vec![])` to `md`.
// If you pass content like the example below to `Document::from`,
// `html5ever` will create a `<head>` element and place your `<style>` element inside it.
// To preserve the original order, use `Document::fragment`.
let contents = "<style>p {color: blue;}</style>\
<div><h1>Content Heading<h1></div>\
<p>I really like using Markdown.</p>\
<p>I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.</p>";
let expected = "p \\{color: blue;\\}\n\
I really like using Markdown\\.\n\n\
I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on\\.";
let doc = fragment;
let got = doc.md;
assert_eq!;
